Below is a quick “ready‑to‑run” example that will pull up to 10 file reports from VirusTotal for all samples that communicated with **12.234.56.126**. It uses the official Vt v3 REST interface – simply replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your real key (`my_api`) before running. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # # Query VirusTotal for files that contacted IP 12.234.56.126 # • limit : maximum results per page (≤100) # • cursor: pointer returned by previous calls when paging through data # IP="12.234.56.126" LIMIT=10 # Max items per page (you said 10) CURSOR="pointer" # Continuation token supplied by VT after first run APIKEY="my_api" # <-- put your actual key here BASE_URL="https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3" # Build URL with optional parameters QUERY="${BASE_URL}/ip_addresses/${IP}/files?limit=${LIMIT}" [ ! -z "$CURSOR" ] && QUERY+="&cursor=$CURSOR" echo "Requesting: $QUERY" HTTP_STATUS=$(curl --silent \ --write-out "%{http_code}" \ --output /tmp/vt_response.json \ -H "x-apikey: ${APIKEY}" \ "${QUERY}") if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" != "200" ]; then echo "❌ Error: HTTP status $HTTP_STATUS" cat /tmp/vt_response.json >&2 else echo "✅ Success! Response stored at /tmp/vt_response.json" fi ``` ### What does the script do? | Step | Description | |------|-------------| | 1️⃣ | Builds the full URI `/ip_addresses//files`. | | 2️⃣ | Adds two query params:
• `limit`: caps the result set to *N* entries.
• `cursor`: tells VT where to resume fetching records. | | 3️⃣ | Sends a signed GET request with header `x-apikey`. | | 4️⃣ | Stores raw JSON into `/tmp/vt_response.json`, prints success/failure. | --- #### Quick notes & best practices | Topic | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Keep your key safe** | Never commit `api_key` to public repos or share it openly. Store it in environment variables or secure vaults. | | **Rate limits** | Free tier → ~4 requests/minute. Paid tiers allow higher throughput. If you hit rate limits, add delays between successive queries. | | **Pagination** | After each successful response, look for `"links": { "next": "" }` or `"pagination": {"cursor":"", ...}`. Use the new cursor value for subsequent runs until there’s none left. | | **Error handling** | A non‑200 status means something went wrong—check the body for error details. Common errors include invalid API key, exceeded quota, or malformed request. | | **Data extraction** | Once you have the JSON, parse fields like `data[*].attributes.*` to see hash values, detection counts, etc., and feed those into your own database or analytics pipeline. | Feel free to adapt the above Bash snippet into whatever scripting language you prefer (Python, PowerShell, Go, …) – the core logic stays identical. Happy hunting!
